title: Remaining Resort Lift-Pass Product Curation
summary: Reviewed the remaining Snowcast destinations that were not part of the recent Hintertux, Tignes, Val d'Isere, Chamonix, or Zell am See-Kaprun curation passes. Added one source-backed default lift-pass product per remaining destination, added the shared Matterhorn Ski Paradise terrain domain for Zermatt and Cervinia, and left weakly sourced lodging/rental estimate fields unchanged.

validation_commands: UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run --no-config python -m app.data.compare_ranking --output-dir artifacts/ranking-comparison
ranking_comparison_summary: Ran `UV_CACHE_DIR=.uv-cache uv run --no-config python -m app.data.compare_ranking --output-dir artifacts/ranking-comparison`; output had 12 rows across 11 result groups. Existing scenarios exercised several remaining destinations and continued to use `terrain_source_scope=ski_area` where child terrain metrics remain unresolved; the new Matterhorn shared domain was not covered by the current representative scenarios.
unresolved_caveats: This pass-product sweep does not promote lodging prices, stay-base quality tiers, supported skill levels, or rental price-quality fields; those remain estimates pending a dedicated sampling policy.

Many official ticket systems use dynamic pricing. The catalog includes representative price examples only where official pages exposed stable values; dynamic-only products keep an empty prices list rather than inventing static amounts.

Shared terrain domains were added only for Matterhorn Ski Paradise and Paradiski because both include multiple modeled Snowcast destinations. Wider regional networks with many unmodeled areas remain pass-product external summaries.
